def can_hit_all_targets(N, targets):
    # Sort targets by x-coordinate
    targets.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
    
    # Try placing the first shot along the line formed by the first and last target
    first_shot_line = (targets[0][1] - targets[-1][1]) / (targets[0][0] - targets[-1][0])
    first_shot_intercept = targets[0][1] - first_shot_line * targets[0][0]
    
    # Count how many targets are covered by the first shot
    covered_by_first_shot = sum(1 for x, y in targets if abs(y - (first_shot_line * x + first_shot_intercept)) < 1e-9)
    
    # If all targets are covered by the first shot, return success
    if covered_by_first_shot == N:
        return "success"
    
    # Sort remaining targets by y-coordinate
    remaining_targets = [target for target in targets if target != targets[0] and target != targets[-1]]
    remaining_targets.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
    
    # Try placing the second shot along the line formed by the first and last of the remaining targets
    second_shot_line = (remaining_targets[0][1] - remaining_targets[-1][1]) / (remaining_targets[0][0] - remaining_targets[-1][0])
    second_shot_intercept = remaining_targets[0][1] - second_shot_line * remaining_targets[0][0]
    
    # Count how many targets are covered by the second shot

    # If all remaining targets are covered by the second shot, return success
    if covered_by_second_shot == len(remaining_targets):
        return "success"
    
    # Otherwise, return failure
    return "failure"
